This vignette shows how to wire `statci` into reproducible research repositories and R packages using declarative `.statci.yml` project configuration, `statci_audit_project()`, SARIF 2.1.0 GitHub Code Scanning annotations, and hardened GitHub Actions workflows.

```{r setup}
library(statci)
```

## 1. Declarative Project Configuration with `.statci.yml`

`read_statci_config()` parses `.statci.yml` with `eval.expr = FALSE` (preventing arbitrary R code evaluation during YAML loading) and validates every rule ID, severity override, relative path, report format, and CI gate setting:

```{r config-demo}
tmp_proj <- tempfile("statci_ci_demo_")
dir.create(file.path(tmp_proj, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(tmp_proj, "models"), recursive = TRUE)

# Write a clean analysis script and a saved model + manuscript
clean_src <- system.file("examples", "clean-analysis.R", package = "statci")
if (nzchar(clean_src)) {
  file.copy(clean_src, file.path(tmp_proj, "R", "analysis.R"))
} else {
  writeLines(c("set.seed(2026)", "x <- rnorm(50)"), file.path(tmp_proj, "R", "analysis.R"))
}

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
saveRDS(list(primary = fit), file.path(tmp_proj, "models", "fits.rds"))

writeLines(c(
  "<!-- statci: model=primary term=wt -->",
  "Vehicle weight predicted MPG (*b* = -5.34, SE = 0.56, *p* < .001, *N* = 32)."
), file.path(tmp_proj, "manuscript.qmd"))

writeLines(c(
  "version: 1",
  "lint:",
  "  paths: [R]",
  "  exclude_rules: [cor_without_use_arg]",
  "  severity_overrides:",
  "    short_logical_literal: error",
  "manuscript:",
  "  path: manuscript.qmd",
  "  models: models/fits.rds",
  "gate:",
  "  fail_on: fail",
  "report:",
  "  title: \"Automated Study CI Audit\"",
  "  output_dir: statci-reports",
  "  formats: [html, markdown, sarif]"
), file.path(tmp_proj, ".statci.yml"))

cfg <- read_statci_config(file.path(tmp_proj, ".statci.yml"))
cfg
```

## 2. One-Call Project Orchestration (`statci_audit_project()`)

`statci_audit_project()` discovers `.statci.yml`, runs AST linting with project severity overrides, audits the configured manuscript, writes HTML/Markdown/SARIF artifacts, and enforces the quality gate:

```{r orchestrate}
proj_rep <- statci_audit_project(tmp_proj, enforce_gate = TRUE)
proj_rep
basename(proj_rep$artifacts)
```

## 3. SARIF 2.1.0 Export for GitHub Code Scanning

`export_statci_sarif()` converts AST lint diagnostics into standard SARIF 2.1.0 JSON so findings appear directly as inline annotations on pull-request diffs in GitHub Code Scanning:

```{r sarif-demo}
flawed_lint <- stat_lint_text("x <- rnorm(10)\nm <- mean(x, na.rm = T)\n")
sarif_txt <- export_statci_sarif(flawed_lint)
sarif_obj <- jsonlite::fromJSON(sarif_txt)
list(
  version = sarif_obj$version,
  tool = sarif_obj$runs$tool$driver$name,
  n_results = nrow(sarif_obj$runs$results[[1]])
)
```

## 4. Generating Hardened GitHub Actions Workflows

`use_statci_github_action()` generates a security-hardened `.github/workflows/statci.yaml` that:
- Validates all branch names, R versions, and project-relative paths against YAML/shell/R injection;
- Passes all configuration via workflow `env:` variables with zero untrusted string interpolation in `run:`;
- Pins action versions and disables checkout credential persistence (`persist-credentials: false`);
- Optionally enables SARIF 2.1.0 upload to GitHub Code Scanning (`upload_sarif = TRUE`).

```{r gha-gen}
wf <- use_statci_github_action(
  path = tmp_proj,
  branches = c("main"),
  r_version = "release",
  lint_paths = c("R"),
  manuscript = "manuscript.qmd",
  models_path = "models/fits.rds",
  upload_sarif = TRUE
)
cat(head(readLines(wf), 34), sep = "\n")

unlink(tmp_proj, recursive = TRUE)
```
